title: Gemini 4 Neon on iac-bench 2026-11
summary: How Gemini 4 Neon did on iac-bench 2026-11: an overall composite of 80.4, scores per fixture, strengths, weaknesses and the patterns in its OpenTofu modules.

## Summary


Gemini 4 Neon ranks 12th of 24 with an overall composite of 80.4, the highest of the six Google models. It is one of nine models with no security finding in any of its 18 attempts, and the only Google model among them. Its gap to Kimi K3.1 Pro (81.1, one place above) is within the margin of three samples (win probability 0.28). It is ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon, Qwen4 Max and Gemini 4 Hydrogen with win probabilities 0.97, 0.89 and 0.96.


On five fixtures its medians are 83.1–89.8, and its best attempt (App Service) scores 96.1. G004 is the exception at 43.5: all three Aurora modules have Secrets Manager manage the master password on member clusters of the global database, a known apply failure that halves the composite. Without the multiplier those three attempts would score about 82–89.


Its modules hardcode the security posture and include almost every expertise item the benchmark checks. Their weakness is size: a concept input such as a workload profile, plus an override input for each value it sets, gives it the largest interfaces in the field on three fixtures, and the interface budget is lost in 16/18 attempts.

## Strengths


- **No security finding in 18/18 attempts.**


- App Service: HTTPS-only and disabled basic-auth publishing are literals on the app and the slot (` H1` and` H2` at full credit in 3/3).
- Storage account: blob public access and shared-key access are off with no input to turn them on (G006` H1` ,` H2` in 3/3).
- GKE: nodes have no public IP and no input can give them one (G005` H2` , 3/3).


- **Expertise items nearly complete.**


- 7/7 on S3 and 9/9 on Cloud SQL in every attempt. That includes backups that survive instance deletion (G002` E1` ), found in 6 of 71 field attempts; three of them are Gemini 4 Neon's.
- 5/5 on App Service in 3/3, including Key Vault references (` E5` , 16/72 field-wide).
- One Aurora attempt finds all 8 G004 expertise items, including the engine version lookup and member versions that follow the global cluster.


- **Cloud SQL graded 100 by the judge in 3/3.** Consumer` database_flags` are merged before the module's security flags, so IAM authentication and audit logging cannot be turned off.
- **Validation everywhere.** 17–35` validation` blocks per module (449 across 18), plus preconditions such as refusing` force_destroy` in production and rejecting wildcard CORS origins with write methods.
- **Clean mechanics.** *Lifecycle meta-arguments* , *Deprecated patterns* , *Outputs* and *Sensitive values* scored 2 in 18/18; *Internal logic* , *Scope* and *File layout* in 17/18.


## Weaknesses


- **G004 known apply failure, 3/3.**` manage_master_user_password = true` on member clusters (F1), so the composite is halved and` H9` is lost in 3/3. In two of them extra cluster parameters are merged after the defaults, so a consumer can override` rds.force_ssl` ( *Anti-patterns* 0). The same modules have 47–52 inputs against a budget of 12–22 (` A5` lost in 3/3), and two of three skip the final snapshot (` H12` ).
- **Interface size.** Budget items lost in 16/18 attempts: S3 33–41 inputs (budget 8–16), GKE 24–41 (11–21), storage account 20–32 (9–17), Cloud SQL 30–36 (25–35). The judge gave *Interface design* 1 in 13/18.
- **Exposure knobs the judge flagged.**


- GKE: one attempt's` enable_private_endpoint` and` gcp_public_cidrs_access_enabled` can open the API server ( *Anti-patterns* 0); another lets` security_posture_mode` and` vulnerability_scanning_mode` be set to disabled values; a third accepts` 0.0.0.0/0` in an unvalidated` authorized_networks` .
- Storage account: one attempt's` network_default_action` accepts` Allow` , overriding the module's default-Deny firewall ( *Anti-patterns* 0).
- App Service:` minimum_tls_version` is an input in 2/3, losing` H3` .


- **S3 extras and gaps.** CloudFront access grants in 3/3 (` A4` ); EventBridge notifications and bucket metrics judged out of scope in one attempt ( *Scope* 1); no provider block with a configurable region (` H15` , 3/3); tags applied per resource rather than through` default_tags` (` H12` half credit, 3/3).
- **Cloud SQL data protection.**` H3` at half credit in 3/3, no` deletion_policy` that keeps removed databases in 2/3 (` H11` ), and the region reaches the instance but not the provider (` H9` half credit, 3/3).
- **Provider constraints that admit a new major** (` >= 6.0` and similar) in 9/18 attempts (` B1` ).


## Characteristic patterns


- **Profiles with overrides.** On S3 every attempt adds a` workload_type` ,` use_case` or` workload_profile` input, then a null-default override for each lifecycle value the profile sets (excerpt below).
- **The largest interfaces in the field** on S3 (median 34), Aurora (48) and GKE (37), and the second largest on Cloud SQL (32). App Service is the exception at 17.
- **Long outputs.** 939,901 output tokens across 18 attempts, second only to GLM-5.3.
- **Two inaccurate descriptions** ( *Documentation* 0 in 2/18): a GKE comment about` initial_node_count = 0` replacing a deprecated flag, and an App Service resource group name that the code builds differently.
- **Leftover structure in one attempt.** An Aurora module ships an empty` modules/regional-cluster/` directory of nine empty files ( *File layout* 1).
- **READMEs in 9/18 attempts,** none on Cloud SQL or Aurora.


## Representative excerpt


` G001/gemini-4-neon-e3/locals.tf` lines 73–78


```text
profile = local.workload_profiles[var.workload_profile]


versioning_enabled                     = var.versioning_enabled != null ? var.versioning_enabled : local.profile.versioning_enabled
object_expiration_days                 = var.object_expiration_days != null ? var.object_expiration_days : local.profile.object_expiration_days
noncurrent_version_expiration_days     = var.noncurrent_version_expiration_days != null ? var.noncurrent_version_expiration_days : local.profile.noncurrent_version_expiration_days
abort_incomplete_multipart_upload_days = var.abort_incomplete_multipart_upload_days != null ? var.abort_incomplete_multipart_upload_days : local.profile.abort_incomplete_multipart_upload_days


```


A workload profile chosen by one concept input sets the lifecycle defaults, and every value it sets also has its own override input. The profile suits app developers new to S3; the overrides are why its S3 modules have 33–41 inputs against a budget of 8–16.
